groups.instructions: Choose the correct option to complete each sentence. The questions get harder as you go.

questions.prompt: My brother ______ in a bank in the city centre.
questions.explanation: A2. Present simple with he/she/it adds -s: works.

questions.prompt: We ______ to the beach last weekend.
questions.explanation: A2. 'Last weekend' is a finished past time, so the past simple 'went' is used.

questions.prompt: There isn't ______ milk left in the fridge.
questions.explanation: A2. 'Any' is used in negative sentences with uncountable nouns.

questions.prompt: This exercise is ______ than the last one.
questions.explanation: A2. Two-syllable adjectives ending in -y change to -ier: easier.
B1. 'Since' + a past point up to now takes the present perfect.

questions.prompt: If it ______ tomorrow, we will cancel the picnic.
questions.explanation: B1. First conditional: if + present simple, will + verb.

questions.prompt: She was cooking dinner when the phone ______.
questions.explanation: B1. A short action (past simple) interrupts a longer one (past continuous).

questions.prompt: The man ______ car was stolen called the police.
questions.explanation: B1. 'Whose' shows possession: the man's car.

questions.prompt: This bridge ______ in 1932 by a team of local engineers.
questions.explanation: B1. The bridge receives the action ('by a team ...'), so the past simple passive is needed: was + past participle.

questions.prompt: I'm not used to ______ up so early.
questions.explanation: B2. In 'be used to', 'to' is a preposition, so it is followed by an -ing form.

questions.prompt: If I had known about the traffic, I ______ earlier.
questions.explanation: B2. Third conditional: if + past perfect, would have + past participle.

questions.prompt: ______ the heavy rain, the match went ahead as planned.
questions.explanation: B2. 'Despite' is followed by a noun phrase. 'Although' and 'even though' need a clause with a verb.

questions.prompt: By the time we arrived at the cinema, the film ______.
questions.explanation: B2. The past perfect shows that one past event happened before another (arrived).

questions.prompt: Not until the results were published ______ how serious the problem was.
questions.explanation: C1. After a negative expression such as 'Not until ...' at the start of a sentence, the subject and auxiliary are inverted: did people realise.

questions.prompt: It is essential that every applicant ______ a copy of their passport.
questions.explanation: C1. After 'It is essential/vital/important that ...', formal English uses the subjunctive: the base form of the verb, with no -s.
